CAT.1.1.en: For the purposes of this Convention, the term "torture" means any act by which severe pain or suffering, whether physical or mental, is intentionally inflicted on a person for such purposes as obtaining from him or a third person information or a confession, punishing him for an act he or a third person has committed or is suspected of having committed, or intimidating or coercing him or a third person, or for any reason based on discrimination of any kind, when such pain or suffering is inflicted by or at the instigation of or with the consent or acquiescence of a public official or other person acting in an official capacity. It does not include pain or suffering arising only from, inherent in or incidental to lawful sanctions.

CAT.15.en: Each State Party shall ensure that any statement which is established to have been made as a result of torture shall not be invoked as evidence in any proceedings, except against a person accused of torture as evidence that the statement was made.

CAT.16.1.en: Each State Party shall undertake to prevent in any territory under its jurisdiction other acts of cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment which do not amount to torture as defined in article I, when such acts are committed by or at the instigation of or with the consent or acquiescence of a public official or other person acting in an official capacity. In particular, the obligations contained in articles 10, 11, 12 and 13 shall apply with the substitution for references to torture of references to other forms of cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.

CAT.2.1.en: Each State Party shall take effective legislative, administrative, judicial or other measures to prevent acts of torture in any territory under its jurisdiction.

CED.1.1.en: No one shall be subjected to enforced disappearance.

CED.17.1.en: No one shall be held in secret detention.

CED.2.en: For the purposes of this Convention, “enforced disappearance” is considered to be the arrest, detention, abduction or any other form of deprivation of liberty by agents of the State or by persons or groups of persons acting with the authorization, support or acquiescence of the State, followed by a refusal to acknowledge the deprivation of liberty or by concealment of the fate or whereabouts of the disappeared person, which place such a person outside the protection of the law.

CED.5.en: The widespread or systematic practice of enforced disappearance constitutes a crime against humanity as defined in applicable international law and shall attract the consequences provided for under such applicable international law.

CEDAW.1.en: For the purposes of the present Convention, the term "discrimination against women" shall mean any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of impairing or nullifying the recognition, enjoyment or exercise by women, irrespective of their marital status, on a basis of equality of men and women, of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field.

CEDAW.15.en:
1. States Parties shall accord to women equality with men before the law.

2. States Parties shall accord to women, in civil matters, a legal capacity identical to that of men and the same opportunities to exercise that capacity. In particular, they shall give women equal rights to conclude contracts and to administer property and shall treat them equally in all stages of procedure in courts and tribunals.

3. States Parties agree that all contracts and all other private instruments of any kind with a legal effect which is directed at restricting the legal capacity of women shall be deemed null and void.

4. States Parties shall accord to men and women the same rights with regard to the law relating to the movement of persons and the freedom to choose their residence and domicile.

CRC.19.1.en: States Parties shall take all appropriate legislative, administrative, social and educational measures to protect the child from all forms of physical or mental violence, injury or abuse, neglect or negligent treatment, maltreatment or exploitation, including sexual abuse, while in the care of parent(s), legal guardian(s) or any other person who has the care of the child.

CRC.2.1.en: States Parties shall respect and ensure the rights set forth in the present Convention to each child within their jurisdiction without discrimination of any kind, irrespective of the child's or his or her parent's or legal guardian's race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national, ethnic or social origin, property, disability, birth or other status.

CRC.3.1.en: In all actions concerning children, whether undertaken by public or private social welfare institutions, courts of law, administrative authorities or legislative bodies, the best interests of the child shall be a primary consideration.

CRPD.12.2.en: States Parties shall recognize that persons with disabilities enjoy legal capacity on an equal basis with others in all aspects of life.

CRPD.5.1.en: States Parties recognize that all persons are equal before and under the law and are entitled without any discrimination to the equal protection and equal benefit of the law.

GENOCIDE.1.en: The Contracting Parties confirm that genocide, whether committed in time of peace or in time of war, is a crime under international law which they undertake to prevent and to punish.

GENOCIDE.4.en: Persons committing genocide or any of the other acts enumerated in article III shall be punished, whether they are constitutionally responsible rulers, public officials or private individuals.

ICCPR.1.1.en: All peoples have the right of self-determination. By virtue of that right they freely determine their political status and freely pursue their economic, social and cultural development.

ICCPR.1.2.en: All peoples may, for their own ends, freely dispose of their natural wealth and resources without prejudice to any obligations arising out of international economic co-operation, based upon the principle of mutual benefit, and international law. In no case may a people be deprived of its own means of subsistence.

ICCPR.10.1.en: All persons deprived of their liberty shall be treated with humanity and with respect for the inherent dignity of the human person.

ICCPR.12.1.en: Everyone lawfully within the territory of a State shall, within that territory, have the right to liberty of movement and freedom to choose his residence.

ICCPR.12.2.en: Everyone shall be free to leave any country, including his own.

ICCPR.12.3.en: The above-mentioned rights shall not be subject to any restrictions except those which are provided by law, are necessary to protect national security, public order (ordre public), public health or morals or the rights and freedoms of others, and are consistent with the other rights recognized in the present Covenant.

ICCPR.14.1.en: All persons shall be equal before the courts and tribunals. In the determination of any criminal charge against him, or of his rights and obligations in a suit at law, everyone shall be entitled to a fair and public hearing by a competent, independent and impartial tribunal established by law. The press and the public may be excluded from all or part of a trial for reasons of morals, public order (ordre public) or national security in a democratic society, or when the interest of the private lives of the parties so requires, or to the extent strictly necessary in the opinion of the court in special circumstances where publicity would prejudice the interests of justice; but any judgement rendered in a criminal case or in a suit at law shall be made public except where the interest of juvenile persons otherwise requires or the proceedings concern matrimonial disputes or the guardianship of children.

ICCPR.14.2.en: Everyone charged with a criminal offence shall have the right to be presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law.

ICCPR.15.2.en: Nothing in this article shall prejudice the trial and punishment of any person for any act or omission which, at the time when it was committed, was criminal according to the general principles of law recognized by the community of nations.

ICCPR.17.1.en: No one shall be subjected to arbitrary or unlawful interference with his privacy, family, home or correspondence, nor to unlawful attacks on his honour and reputation.

ICCPR.17.2.en: Everyone has the right to the protection of the law against such interference or attacks.

ICCPR.18.1.en: Everyone shall have the right to freedom of thought, conscience and religion. This right shall include freedom to have or to adopt a religion or belief of his choice, and freedom, either individually or in community with others and in public or private, to manifest his religion or belief in worship, observance, practice and teaching.

ICCPR.18.2.en: No one shall be subject to coercion which would impair his freedom to have or to adopt a religion or belief of his choice.

ICCPR.18.3.en: Freedom to manifest one's religion or beliefs may be subject only to such limitations as are prescribed by law and are necessary to protect public safety, order, health, or morals or the fundamental rights and freedoms of others.

ICCPR.19.1.en: Everyone shall have the right to hold opinions without interference.

ICCPR.19.2.en: Everyone shall have the right to freedom of expression; this right shall include freedom to seek, receive and impart information and ideas of all kinds, regardless of frontiers, either orally, in writing or in print, in the form of art, or through any other media of his choice.

ICCPR.2.1.en: Each State Party to the present Covenant undertakes to respect and to ensure to all individuals within its territory and subject to its jurisdiction the rights recognized in the present Covenant, without distinction of any kind, such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

ICCPR.20.1.en: Any propaganda for war shall be prohibited by law.

ICCPR.20.2.en: Any advocacy of national, racial or religious hatred that constitutes incitement to discrimination, hostility or violence shall be prohibited by law.

ICCPR.21.en: The right of peaceful assembly shall be recognized. No restrictions may be placed on the exercise of this right other than those imposed in conformity with the law and which are necessary in a democratic society in the interests of national security or public safety, public order (ordre public), the protection of public health or morals or the protection of the rights and freedoms of others.

ICCPR.22.1.en: Everyone shall have the right to freedom of association with others, including the right to form and join trade unions for the protection of his interests.

ICCPR.22.2.en: No restrictions may be placed on the exercise of this right other than those which are prescribed by law and which are necessary in a democratic society in the interests of national security or public safety, public order (ordre public), the protection of public health or morals or the protection of the rights and freedoms of others. This article shall not prevent the imposition of lawful restrictions on members of the armed forces and of the police in their exercise of this right.

ICCPR.23.2.en: The right of men and women of marriageable age to marry and to found a family shall be recognized.

ICCPR.23.3.en: No marriage shall be entered into without the free and full consent of the intending spouses.

ICCPR.23.4.en: States Parties to the present Covenant shall take appropriate steps to ensure equality of rights and responsibilities of spouses as to marriage, during marriage and at its dissolution. In the case of dissolution, provision shall be made for the necessary protection of any children.

ICCPR.24.1.en: Every child shall have, without any discrimination as to race, colour, sex, language, religion, national or social origin, property or birth, the right to such measures of protection as are required by his status as a minor, on the part of his family, society and the State.

ICCPR.26.en: All persons are equal before the law and are entitled without any discrimination to the equal protection of the law. In this respect, the law shall prohibit any discrimination and guarantee to all persons equal and effective protection against discrimination on any ground such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

ICCPR.27.en: In those States in which ethnic, religious or linguistic minorities exist, persons belonging to such minorities shall not be denied the right, in community with the other members of their group, to enjoy their own culture, to profess and practise their own religion, or to use their own language.

ICCPR.3.en: The States Parties to the present Covenant undertake to ensure the equal right of men and women to the enjoyment of all civil and political rights set forth in the present Covenant.

ICCPR.4.2.en: No derogation from articles 6, 7, 8 (paragraphs I and 2), 11, 15, 16 and 18 may be made under this provision.

ICCPR.4.3.en: Any State Party to the present Covenant availing itself of the right of derogation shall immediately inform the other States Parties to the present Covenant, through the intermediary of the Secretary- General of the United Nations, of the provisions from which it has derogated and of the reasons by which it was actuated. A further communication shall be made, through the same intermediary, on the date on which it terminates such derogation.

ICCPR.6.1.en: Every human being has the inherent right to life. This right shall be protected by law. No one shall be arbitrarily deprived of his life.

ICCPR.6.2.en: In countries which have not abolished the death penalty, sentence of death may be imposed only for the most serious crimes in accordance with the law in force at the time of the commission of the crime and not contrary to the provisions of the present Covenant and to the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide. This penalty can only be carried out pursuant to a final judgement rendered by a competent court.

ICCPR.6.5.en: Sentence of death shall not be imposed for crimes committed by persons below eighteen years of age and shall not be carried out on pregnant women.

ICCPR.7.en: No one shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. In particular, no one shall be subjected without his free consent to medical or scientific experimentation.

ICCPR.8.1.en: No one shall be held in slavery; slavery and the slave-trade in all their forms shall be prohibited.

ICCPR.9.1.en: Everyone has the right to liberty and security of person. No one shall be subjected to arbitrary arrest or detention. No one shall be deprived of his liberty except on such grounds and in accordance with such procedure as are established by law.

ICCPR.9.3.en: Anyone arrested or detained on a criminal charge shall be brought promptly before a judge or other officer authorized by law to exercise judicial power and shall be entitled to trial within a reasonable time or to release. It shall not be the general rule that persons awaiting trial shall be detained in custody, but release may be subject to guarantees to appear for trial, at any other stage of the judicial proceedings, and, should occasion arise, for execution of the judgement.

ICCPR.9.4.en: Anyone who is deprived of his liberty by arrest or detention shall be entitled to take proceedings before a court, in order that that court may decide without delay on the lawfulness of his detention and order his release if the detention is not lawful.

ICCPR.9.5.en: Anyone who has been the victim of unlawful arrest or detention shall have an enforceable right to compensation.

ICERD.1.1.en: In this Convention, the term "racial discrimination" shall mean any distinction, exclusion, restriction or preference based on race, colour, descent, or national or ethnic origin which has the purpose or effect of nullifying or impairing the recognition, enjoyment or exercise, on an equal footing, of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural or any other field of public life.

ICESCR.1.1.en: All peoples have the right of self-determination. By virtue of that right they freely determine their political status and freely pursue their economic, social and cultural development.

ICESCR.11.1.en: The States Parties to the present Covenant recognize the right of everyone to an adequate standard of living for himself and his family, including adequate food, clothing and housing, and to the continuous improvement of living conditions. The States Parties will take appropriate steps to ensure the realization of this right, recognizing to this effect the essential importance of international co-operation based on free consent.

ICESCR.12.1.en: The States Parties to the present Covenant recognize the right of everyone to the enjoyment of the highest attainable standard of physical and mental health.

ICESCR.13.1.en: The States Parties to the present Covenant recognize the right of everyone to education. They agree that education shall be directed to the full development of the human personality and the sense of its dignity, and shall strengthen the respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. They further agree that education shall enable all persons to participate effectively in a free society, promote understanding, tolerance and friendship among all nations and all racial, ethnic or religious groups, and further the activities of the United Nations for the maintenance of peace.

ICESCR.13.3.en: The States Parties to the present Covenant undertake to have respect for the liberty of parents and, when applicable, legal guardians to choose for their children schools, other than those established by the public authorities, which conform to such minimum educational standards as may be laid down or approved by the State and to ensure the religious and moral education of their children in conformity with their own convictions.

ICESCR.3.en: The States Parties to the present Covenant undertake to ensure the equal right of men and women to the enjoyment of all economic, social and cultural rights set forth in the present Covenant.

ICESCR.6.1.en: The States Parties to the present Covenant recognize the right to work, which includes the right of everyone to the opportunity to gain his living by work which he freely chooses or accepts, and will take appropriate steps to safeguard this right.

ICESCR.9.en: The States Parties to the present Covenant recognize the right of everyone to social security, including social insurance.

ROME.27.en:
1. This Statute shall apply equally to all persons without any distinction based on official capacity. In particular, official capacity as a Head of State or Government, a member of a Government or parliament, an elected representative or a government official shall in no case exempt a person from criminal responsibility under this Statute, nor shall it, in and of itself, constitute a ground for reduction of sentence.

2. Immunities or special procedural rules which may attach to the official capacity of a person, whether under national or international law, shall not bar the Court from exercising its jurisdiction over such a person.

UDHR.10.en: Everyone is entitled in full equality to a fair and public hearing by an independent and impartial tribunal, in the determination of his rights and obligations and of any criminal charge against him.

UDHR.11.1.en: Everyone charged with a penal offence has the right to be presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law in a public trial at which he has had all the guarantees necessary for his defence.

UDHR.11.2.en: No one shall be held guilty of any penal offence on account of any act or omission which did not constitute a penal offence, under national or international law, at the time when it was committed. Nor shall a heavier penalty be imposed than the one that was applicable at the time the penal offence was committed.

UDHR.12.en: No one shall be subjected to arbitrary interference with his privacy, family, home or correspondence, nor to attacks upon his honour and reputation. Everyone has the right to the protection of the law against such interference or attacks.

UDHR.13.1.en: Everyone has the right to freedom of movement and residence within the borders of each state.

UDHR.13.2.en: Everyone has the right to leave any country, including his own, and to return to his country.

UDHR.14.1.en: Everyone has the right to seek and to enjoy in other countries asylum from persecution.

UDHR.15.1.en: Everyone has the right to a nationality.

UDHR.15.2.en: No one shall be arbitrarily deprived of his nationality nor denied the right to change his nationality.

UDHR.16.1.en: Men and women of full age, without any limitation due to race, nationality or religion, have the right to marry and to found a family. They are entitled to equal rights as to marriage, during marriage and at its dissolution.

UDHR.16.2.en: Marriage shall be entered into only with the free and full consent of the intending spouses.

UDHR.16.3.en: The family is the natural and fundamental group unit of society and is entitled to protection by society and the State.

UDHR.18.en: Everyone has the right to freedom of thought, conscience and religion; this right includes freedom to change his religion or belief, and freedom, either alone or in community with others and in public or private, to manifest his religion or belief in teaching, practice, worship and observance.

UDHR.19.en: Everyone has the right to freedom of opinion and expression; this right includes freedom to hold opinions without interference and to seek, receive and impart information and ideas through any media and regardless of frontiers.

UDHR.2.en: Everyone is entitled to all the rights and freedoms set forth in this Declaration, without distinction of any kind, such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status. Furthermore, no distinction shall be made on the basis of the political, jurisdictional or international status of the country or territory to which a person belongs, whether it be independent, trust, non-self-governing or under any other limitation of sovereignty.

UDHR.20.en:
1. Everyone has the right to freedom of peaceful assembly and association.

2. No one may be compelled to belong to an association.

UDHR.20.1.en: Everyone has the right to freedom of peaceful assembly and association.

UDHR.21.1.en: Everyone has the right to take part in the government of his country, directly or through freely chosen representatives.

UDHR.21.2.en: Everyone has the right of equal access to public service in his country.

UDHR.21.3.en: The will of the people shall be the basis of the authority of government; this will shall be expressed in periodic and genuine elections which shall be by universal and equal suffrage and shall be held by secret vote or by equivalent free voting procedures.

UDHR.22.en: Everyone, as a member of society, has the right to social security and is entitled to realization, through national effort and international co-operation and in accordance with the organization and resources of each State, of the economic, social and cultural rights indispensable for his dignity and the free development of his personality.

UDHR.23.1.en: Everyone has the right to work, to free choice of employment, to just and favourable conditions of work and to protection against unemployment.

UDHR.23.2.en: Everyone, without any discrimination, has the right to equal pay for equal work.

UDHR.23.4.en: Everyone has the right to form and to join trade unions for the protection of his interests.

UDHR.25.1.en: Everyone has the right to a standard of living adequate for the health and well-being of himself and of his family, including food, clothing, housing and medical care and necessary social services, and the right to security in the event of unemployment, sickness, disability, widowhood, old age or other lack of livelihood in circumstances beyond his control.

UDHR.26.1.en: Everyone has the right to education. Education shall be free, at least in the elementary and fundamental stages. Elementary education shall be compulsory. Technical and professional education shall be made generally available and higher education shall be equally accessible to all on the basis of merit.

UDHR.26.2.en: Education shall be directed to the full development of the human personality and to the strengthening of respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. It shall promote understanding, tolerance and friendship among all nations, racial or religious groups, and shall further the activities of the United Nations for the maintenance of peace.

UDHR.26.3.en: Parents have a prior right to choose the kind of education that shall be given to their children.

UDHR.27.1.en: Everyone has the right freely to participate in the cultural life of the community, to enjoy the arts and to share in scientific advancement and its benefits.

UDHR.27.2.en: Everyone has the right to the protection of the moral and material interests resulting from any scientific, literary or artistic production of which he is the author.

UDHR.3.en: Everyone has the right to life, liberty and security of person.

UDHR.4.en: No one shall be held in slavery or servitude; slavery and the slave trade shall be prohibited in all their forms.

UDHR.5.en: No one shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.

UDHR.7.en: All are equal before the law and are entitled without any discrimination to equal protection of the law. All are entitled to equal protection against any discrimination in violation of this Declaration and against any incitement to such discrimination.

UDHR.8.en: Everyone has the right to an effective remedy by the competent national tribunals for acts violating the fundamental rights granted him by the constitution or by law.

UDHR.9.en: No one shall be subjected to arbitrary arrest, detention or exile.

YP.2.A.h: The Rights to Equality and Non-Discrimination
YP.2.A.en: Embody the principles of equality and non-discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation and gender identity in their national constitutions or other appropriate legislation, if not yet incorporated therein, including by means of amendment and interpretation, and ensure the effective realisation of these principles;

YP.2.C.h: The Rights to Equality and Non-Discrimination
YP.2.C.en: Adopt appropriate legislative and other measures to prohibit and eliminate discrimination in the public and private spheres on the basis of sexual orientation and gender identity;

YP.6.B.en: Repeal all laws that criminalise consensual sexual activity among persons of the same sex who are over the age of consent, and ensure that an equal age of consent applies to both same-sex and different-sex sexual activity;

YP10.33.A.h: The Right to Freedom from Criminalisation and Sanction on the Basis of Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity, Gender Expression or Sex Characteristics
YP10.33.A.en: Ensure that legal provisions, including in customary, religious and indigenous laws, whether explicit provisions, or the application of general punitive provisions such as acts against nature, morality, public decency, vagrancy, sodomy and propaganda laws, do not criminalise sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, or establish any form of sanction relating to them;

audits.summary_en: The document contains a recognisable catalogue of civil rights — a ban on inquisition into beliefs, a torture prohibition with exclusion of coerced confessions, presumption of innocence, right of access to courts and counsel, compensation for judicial error, administrative review, free education and universal health and social-security entitlements, an inalienable nationality, and a prohibition of martial law. Nearly all of these, however, are taken back by open-ended conditions: Article 4 makes Islamic criteria supreme over every article of the constitution and all legislation, with the Guardian Council as arbiter, while individual articles add "with observance of Islamic criteria" (women's rights, equality), "detrimental to the fundamentals of Islam" (press, assembly), "Islamic criteria and the interests of the country" (broadcasting), and "except by order of the law" (privacy, arrest, residence, life and property). The most serious contradictions are the entrenchment of an unchangeable official creed with only three recognised religious minorities, the conditioning of non-Muslims' rights on political loyalty, the reservation of the presidency to believing "rijal" with candidate vetting by an unelected body, and the subordination of all three branches to the Leader's absolute guardianship. Judicial rulings on "authoritative fatwas" where statute is silent defeats the legality principle, and enforcement of hudud conflicts with the ban on cruel punishment. The gravest silences are sexual orientation and gender identity, enforced disappearance, incitement and war propaganda, freedom to leave and return to the country, the rights of persons with disabilities and of the child as such, cultural rights, non-derogable rights in emergencies, and any provision on genocide, crimes against humanity or official immunity.
audits.summary_fa: این متن فهرستی از حقوق مدنی را در بر دارد: منع تفتیش عقاید، منع شکنجه و بی‌اعتباری اقرار اجباری، اصل برائت، حق دادخواهی و وکیل، جبران خسارت ناشی از اشتباه قاضی، دیوان عدالت اداری، آموزش رایگان، حق همگانی بهداشت و تأمین اجتماعی، تابعیت غیرقابل‌سلب و ممنوعیت حکومت نظامی. اما تقریباً همه اینها با قیود باز پس گرفته می‌شوند: اصل ۴ موازین اسلامی را بر اطلاق و عموم همه اصول و قوانین حاکم می‌کند و تشخیص را به فقهای شورای نگهبان می‌سپارد، و اصول جداگانه قیودی چون «با رعایت موازین اسلام»، «مخل به مبانی اسلام»، «موازین اسلامی و مصالح کشور» و «مگر به حکم قانون» را می‌افزایند. جدی‌ترین تعارض‌ها عبارت‌اند از تثبیت مذهب رسمی تغییرناپذیر و شناسایی تنها سه اقلیت دینی، مشروط‌کردن حقوق غیرمسلمانان به عدم اقدام علیه نظام، محدودکردن ریاست‌جمهوری به «رجال» معتقد به مذهب رسمی همراه با نظارت استصوابی، و قرار گرفتن هر سه قوه زیر ولایت مطلقه. حکم بر پایه «فتاوای معتبر» در سکوت قانون اصل قانونی بودن جرم را نقض می‌کند و اجرای حدود با منع مجازات‌های ظالمانه ناسازگار است. مهم‌ترین سکوت‌ها: گرایش جنسی و هویت جنسیتی، ناپدیدسازی قهری، منع تحریک به نفرت و تبلیغ جنگ، حق خروج و بازگشت، حقوق افراد دارای معلولیت و حقوق کودک، حقوق فرهنگی، حقوق غیرقابل‌تعلیق در وضعیت اضطراری و هرگونه حکم درباره نسل‌کشی و جنایات علیه بشریت.

review.notes: Published before review at the user's decision (2026-09-25). Quote for «work» corrected from «…نیست برگزید» to the article's «…نیست برگزیند» (art. 28); the «family» quote is article 10 abridged with «…».

equality.quote: ایرانیان زرتشتی، کلیمی و مسیحی تنها اقلیت های دینی شناخته می‌شوند
equality.note_en: Article 19 bars ethnic, racial, colour and language privilege and Article 20 promises equal protection, but only "with observance of Islamic criteria" (a20), only three religious minorities are recognised (a13), decent treatment of non‑Muslims is conditioned on their not acting against Islam (a14), the presidency is reserved for believers in the official creed (a115), and Article 4 subordinates every law to Islamic criteria. This establishes discrimination on religious grounds rather than equal protection.
equality.note_fa: اصل ۱۹ تبعیض قومی و نژادی را نفی می‌کند و اصل ۲۰ از حمایت یکسان قانون سخن می‌گوید، اما مشروط به «رعایت موازین اسلام» است؛ اصل ۱۳ تنها سه اقلیت دینی را می‌شناسد، اصل ۱۴ رعایت حقوق غیرمسلمانان را مشروط می‌کند و اصل ۱۱۵ ریاست‌جمهوری را به معتقدان مذهب رسمی محدود می‌سازد. بنابراین متن تبعیض دینی را نهادینه کرده است.

gender_equality.quote: دولت موظف است حقوق زن را در تمام جهات با رعایت موازین اسلامی تضمین نماید
gender_equality.note_en: Article 3(14) and Article 20 speak of the rights of "men and women" and equality before the law, but Articles 20 and 21 expressly condition women's rights on "Islamic criteria", and Article 4 makes those criteria supreme over all law, leaving family, inheritance and testimony inequalities intact. The presidency is limited to "rijal" (a115), which has been read to exclude women.
gender_equality.note_fa: اصل ۳ بند ۱۴ و اصل ۲۰ از حقوق زن و مرد و تساوی در برابر قانون سخن می‌گویند، اما اصول ۲۰ و ۲۱ آن را به «رعایت موازین اسلام/اسلامی» مشروط می‌کنند و اصل ۴ این موازین را بر همه قوانین حاکم می‌سازد. شرط «رجال» در اصل ۱۱۵ نیز دسترسی زنان به ریاست‌جمهوری را محدود کرده است.

sogi.note_en: The text never mentions sexual orientation or gender identity, and offers no non-discrimination ground covering them; Article 4's supremacy of Islamic criteria over all penal law is the only indirectly relevant clause.
sogi.note_fa: متن هیچ اشاره‌ای به گرایش جنسی یا هویت جنسیتی ندارد و هیچ مبنای عدم تبعیضی برای آنها پیش‌بینی نکرده است؛ تنها اصل ۴ که همه قوانین جزایی را تابع موازین اسلامی می‌کند به‌طور غیرمستقیم مرتبط است.

life.quote: حیثیت، جان، مال، حقوق، مسکن و شغل اشخاص از تعرض مصون است مگر در مواردی که قانون تجویز کند.
life.note_en: Life is protected only "except in cases permitted by law" (a22), and Articles 61 and 156 make the courts responsible for executing the Islamic hudud, with no limitation of the death penalty to the most serious crimes, no bar on execution of juveniles, and pardon available only "within Islamic criteria" (a110.11).
life.note_fa: جان اشخاص تنها «مگر در مواردی که قانون تجویز کند» مصون دانسته شده و اصول ۶۱ و ۱۵۶ اجرای حدود الهی را بر عهده دادگاه‌ها می‌گذارند. هیچ محدودیتی بر مجازات اعدام، منع اعدام کودکان یا حق عفو بدون قید «موازین اسلامی» پیش‌بینی نشده است.

torture.quote: هرگونه شکنجه برای گرفتن اقرار و یا کسب اطلاع ممنوع است.
torture.note_en: Article 38 bans torture but only when used "to obtain a confession or information", and invalidates coerced confessions; Article 39 protects the dignity of detainees. However the ban is narrower than CAT Article 1, and Articles 61 and 156 mandate the enforcement of hudud corporal punishments, which fall under cruel, inhuman or degrading punishment.
torture.note_fa: اصل ۳۸ شکنجه را تنها «برای گرفتن اقرار یا کسب اطلاع» ممنوع می‌کند و اقرار اجباری را بی‌اعتبار می‌داند و اصل ۳۹ هتک حرمت بازداشت‌شدگان را منع می‌کند. اما این تعریف محدودتر از ماده ۱ کنوانسیون منع شکنجه است و اصول ۶۱ و ۱۵۶ اجرای حدود (مجازات‌های بدنی) را تکلیف می‌کنند.

slavery.quote: رعایت آزادی انتخاب شغل، و عدم اجبار افراد به کاری معین و جلوگیری از بهره‌کشی از کار دیگری.
slavery.note_en: Slavery and servitude are never mentioned; the only relevant clause is an economic-policy principle in Article 43(4) against compelling persons to specific work and against exploitation of others' labour, which is not framed as an enforceable individual right.
slavery.note_fa: بردگی و بندگی اصلاً ذکر نشده است؛ تنها بند ۴ اصل ۴۳ به‌عنوان یک اصل سیاست اقتصادی از عدم اجبار افراد به کار معین و منع بهره‌کشی سخن می‌گوید که به‌صورت حق فردی قابل مطالبه تنظیم نشده است.

liberty.quote: هیچ‌کس را نمی‌توان دستگیر کرد مگر به حکم و ترتیبی که قانون معین می‌کند.
liberty.note_en: Article 32 requires a legal basis for arrest, written notice of charges and transfer of the file to judicial authorities within 24 hours, and Article 39 protects detainees' dignity. But there is no habeas corpus procedure, no right to compensation for unlawful detention, and Articles 33 and 39 accept exile "in cases provided by law", contrary to UDHR.9.
liberty.note_fa: اصل ۳۲ دستگیری را منوط به حکم قانون و ابلاغ کتبی اتهام و ارسال پرونده ظرف ۲۴ ساعت می‌کند و اصل ۳۹ حرمت بازداشت‌شدگان را حفظ می‌کند، اما سازوکار اعتراض قضایی به بازداشت و حق جبران خسارت بازداشت غیرقانونی پیش‌بینی نشده و اصول ۳۳ و ۳۹ تبعید «به موجب قانون» را می‌پذیرند.

disappearance.note_en: Enforced disappearance and secret detention are not addressed anywhere; Article 32's 24-hour rule for transmitting the case file is the only partially related safeguard, and there is no register of detainees or family-notification duty.
disappearance.note_fa: ناپدیدسازی قهری و بازداشت مخفی در هیچ اصلی مطرح نشده است؛ تنها مهلت ۲۴ ساعته اصل ۳۲ تا حدی مرتبط است و هیچ تکلیفی به ثبت بازداشت‌شدگان یا اطلاع خانواده وجود ندارد.

fair_trial.quote: با استناد به منابع معتبر اسلامی یا فتاوای معتبر، حکم قضیه را صادر نماید
fair_trial.note_en: Presumption of innocence (a37), counsel (a35), public hearings (a165), reasoned judgments (a166) and non-retroactivity (a169) are stated, but Article 167 obliges judges to decide on "authoritative Islamic sources or fatwas" where statute is silent, defeating legality; judicial qualifications follow fiqh (a163) and the head of the judiciary is appointed by the Leader (a157), weakening independence.
fair_trial.note_fa: اصل برائت (۳۷)، حق وکیل (۳۵)، علنی بودن محاکمات (۱۶۵)، مستدل بودن احکام (۱۶۶) و عطف‌بماسبق نشدن قوانین جزایی (۱۶۹) پیش‌بینی شده‌اند، اما اصل ۱۶۷ قاضی را در سکوت قانون به استناد به «منابع معتبر اسلامی یا فتاوای معتبر» موظف می‌کند که اصل قانونی بودن جرم را نقض می‌کند؛ شرایط قاضی طبق موازین فقهی (۱۶۳) و انتصاب رئیس قوه قضاییه توسط رهبر (۱۵۷) استقلال را تضعیف می‌کند.

remedy.quote: دادخواهی حق مسلم هر فرد است و هر کس می‌تواند به منظور دادخواهی به دادگاه‌های صالح رجوع نماید.
remedy.note_en: Article 34 makes recourse to competent courts an absolute right, Article 171 provides compensation by the State for judicial error, Article 173 creates the Court of Administrative Justice against official acts, and Article 90 allows written complaints against any branch. The remedy structure is stated, though it operates inside the Islamic-criteria framework of Article 4.
remedy.note_fa: اصل ۳۴ دادخواهی را حق مسلم هر فرد می‌داند، اصل ۱۷۱ جبران خسارت ناشی از اشتباه قاضی را پیش‌بینی می‌کند، اصل ۱۷۳ دیوان عدالت اداری را برای شکایت از مأموران دولتی تأسیس می‌کند و اصل ۹۰ امکان شکایت کتبی از هر سه قوه را می‌دهد. سازوکار جبران بیان شده است، هرچند در چارچوب حاکمیت موازین اسلامی اصل ۴ عمل می‌کند.

privacy.quote: سانسور، عدم مخابره و نرساندن آنها، استراق سمع و هر گونه تجسس ممنوع است مگر به حکم قانون.
privacy.note_en: Article 25 forbids opening mail, wiretapping, censorship and any form of spying, and Article 22 protects the home, but both are subject to the open-ended exception "except by order of the law" with no necessity or proportionality test; Article 8 further imposes a mutual duty of enjoining good and forbidding wrong.
privacy.note_fa: اصل ۲۵ بازرسی نامه‌ها، استراق سمع، سانسور و هر گونه تجسس را ممنوع می‌کند و اصل ۲۲ مسکن را مصون می‌داند، اما هر دو با قید باز «مگر به حکم قانون» مشروط شده‌اند و معیار ضرورت و تناسب ندارند؛ اصل ۸ نیز وظیفه متقابل امر به معروف و نهی از منکر را مقرر می‌کند.

movement.quote: می‌تواند به کسانی که پناهندگی سیاسی بخواهند پناه دهد مگر این که بر طبق قوانین ایران خائن و تبهکار شناخته شوند
movement.note_en: Article 33 protects residence and bars exile only "except in cases provided by law"; there is no right to leave or return to the country at all, and asylum in Article 155 is a discretionary power of the state ("may grant") with an exception defined by Iranian law rather than by the political-offence standard.
movement.note_fa: اصل ۳۳ آزادی اقامت و منع تبعید را تنها «مگر در مواردی که قانون مقرر می‌دارد» تضمین می‌کند؛ حق خروج از کشور و بازگشت به آن اصلاً ذکر نشده و پناهندگی در اصل ۱۵۵ یک اختیار دولت («می‌تواند پناه دهد») با استثنای تعریف‌شده در قوانین ایران است.

nationality.quote: تابعیت کشور ایران حق مسلم هر فرد ایرانی و دولت نمی‌تواند از هیچ ایرانی سلب تابعیت کند
nationality.note_en: Article 41 declares Iranian nationality an inalienable right that the state may not withdraw except at the person's own request or on acquisition of another nationality, and Article 42 regulates naturalisation and its withdrawal restrictively. The text says nothing about women's equal right to transmit nationality to children (CEDAW.9).
nationality.note_fa: اصل ۴۱ تابعیت ایرانی را حق مسلم هر ایرانی می‌داند که جز به درخواست خود فرد یا پذیرش تابعیت دیگر سلب نمی‌شود و اصل ۴۲ سلب تابعیت اتباع تحصیل‌شده را محدود می‌کند. درباره حق برابر زنان در انتقال تابعیت به فرزندان چیزی گفته نشده است.

religion.quote: دین رسمی ایران، اسلام و مذهب جعفری اثنی‌عشری است و این اصل الی‌الابد غیر قابل تغییر است
religion.note_en: An unchangeable official creed is established (a12, a177); only Zoroastrians, Jews and Christians are recognised as religious minorities and only "within the limits of the law" (a13); other beliefs (e.g. Baha'is, atheists) are unrecognised; Article 14's decent treatment of non-Muslims is conditional. Article 23 bars inquisition into beliefs but no freedom to change or leave a religion is recognised.
religion.note_fa: مذهب رسمی تغییرناپذیر اعلام شده (اصول ۱۲ و ۱۷۷)، تنها زرتشتیان، کلیمیان و مسیحیان آن هم «در حدود قانون» به‌عنوان اقلیت دینی شناخته می‌شوند (اصل ۱۳) و سایر باورها به رسمیت شناخته نمی‌شوند؛ اصل ۱۴ نیز رعایت حقوق غیرمسلمانان را مشروط می‌کند. اصل ۲۳ تفتیش عقاید را منع می‌کند اما آزادی تغییر دین یا بی‌دینی به رسمیت شناخته نشده است.

expression.quote: نشریات و مطبوعات در بیان مطالب آزادند مگر آن که مخل به مبانی اسلام یا حقوق عمومی باشد.
expression.note_en: Press freedom is granted but withdrawn where publications are "detrimental to the fundamentals of Islam or public rights" (a24), and broadcasting freedom must observe "Islamic criteria and the interests of the country" (a175), with the broadcaster's head appointed by the Leader. These open-ended conditions exceed the limits allowed by ICCPR.19.3.
expression.note_fa: آزادی مطبوعات اعطا شده اما با قید «مخل به مبانی اسلام یا حقوق عمومی» پس گرفته می‌شود (اصل ۲۴) و آزادی بیان در صدا و سیما مشروط به «رعایت موازین اسلامی و مصالح کشور» است (اصل ۱۷۵) که رئیس آن را رهبر منصوب می‌کند. این قیود باز فراتر از محدودیت‌های مجاز در ماده ۱۹(۳) میثاق است.

incitement.note_en: There is no prohibition of war propaganda or of advocacy of national, racial or religious hatred; the text only bars ethnic privilege (a19) and calls for fraternity, without any duty to outlaw incitement.
incitement.note_fa: هیچ ممنوعیتی برای تبلیغ جنگ یا تحریک به نفرت ملی، نژادی و دینی پیش‌بینی نشده است؛ متن تنها امتیاز قومی را نفی می‌کند (اصل ۱۹) و از برادری سخن می‌گوید، بدون تکلیف به جرم‌انگاری تحریک.

assembly.quote: تشکیل اجتماعات و راهپیمایی‌ها، بدون حمل سلاح، به شرط آن که مخل به مبانی اسلام نباشد آزاد است.
assembly.note_en: Peaceful assembly is recognised but conditioned on not being "detrimental to the fundamentals of Islam", an open-ended religious test that is not among the permissible grounds in ICCPR.21.
assembly.note_fa: آزادی اجتماعات و راهپیمایی‌های بدون سلاح به شرط «مخل نبودن به مبانی اسلام» شناخته شده است؛ این قید باز دینی جزو محدودیت‌های مجاز ماده ۲۱ میثاق نیست.

association.quote: آزادند، مشروط به این که اصول استقلال، آزادی، وحدت ملی، موازین اسلامی و اساس جمهوری اسلامی را نقض نکنند
association.note_en: Parties, associations and guilds are free but only if they do not violate "Islamic criteria" and "the foundation of the Islamic Republic" (a26); no one may be compelled to join. Independent trade unions and the right to strike are absent, replaced by state-defined workplace councils (a104).
association.note_fa: احزاب و انجمن‌ها آزادند مشروط به عدم نقض «موازین اسلامی» و «اساس جمهوری اسلامی» (اصل ۲۶) و کسی به عضویت مجبور نمی‌شود. اما از اتحادیه‌های کارگری مستقل و حق اعتصاب خبری نیست و به‌جای آن شوراهای کارگری قانونی (اصل ۱۰۴) پیش‌بینی شده است.

participation.quote: رییس جمهور باید از میان رجال مذهبی و سیاسی که واجد شرایط زیر باشند انتخاب گردد
participation.note_en: Elections for parliament and president are provided (a6, a62, a114), but candidacy is vetted by the unelected Guardian Council (a99, a110.9), the presidency requires belief in the official creed and "rijal" status (a115), and all three branches operate under the Leader's absolute guardianship (a57), who is not popularly elected. Equal access to the highest offices is therefore denied on religious and gender grounds.
participation.note_fa: انتخابات مجلس و ریاست‌جمهوری پیش‌بینی شده است (اصول ۶، ۶۲ و ۱۱۴)، اما صلاحیت نامزدها را شورای نگهبان انتصابی تأیید می‌کند (اصول ۹۹ و ۱۱۰) و ریاست‌جمهوری مشروط به «رجال» بودن و اعتقاد به مذهب رسمی است (اصل ۱۱۵)؛ همه قوا زیر نظر «ولایت مطلقه امر» عمل می‌کنند (اصل ۵۷) که با رأی مستقیم مردم انتخاب نمی‌شود.

self_determination.quote: هم او، انسان را بر سرنوشت اجتماعی خویش حاکم ساخته است. هیچ‌کس نمی‌تواند این حق الهی را از انسان سلب کند
self_determination.note_en: Article 56 declares that God has made man master of his own social destiny and Article 3(8) promises general participation in determining political and economic destiny, but Article 57 places all powers under the absolute guardianship of the jurist, Article 177 makes the Islamic character of the system unamendable, and Article 45 vests public natural wealth in the Islamic government.
self_determination.note_fa: اصل ۵۶ انسان را حاکم بر سرنوشت اجتماعی خویش می‌داند و بند ۸ اصل ۳ مشارکت عامه در تعیین سرنوشت را وعده می‌دهد، اما اصل ۵۷ همه قوا را زیر «ولایت مطلقه امر» قرار می‌دهد، اصل ۱۷۷ اسلامی بودن نظام را تغییرناپذیر می‌کند و اصل ۴۵ ثروت‌های عمومی را در اختیار حکومت اسلامی می‌گذارد.

minorities.quote: استفاده از زبان های محلی و قومی در مطبوعات و رسانه‌های گروهی و تدریس ادبیات آنها در مدارس، در کنار زبان فارسی آزاد است.
minorities.note_en: Local and ethnic languages may be used in the media and their literature taught alongside Persian (a15), Sunni schools of law are respected (a12) and recognised minorities hold reserved seats (a64). But Persian is the compulsory language of official documents and textbooks, Arabic teaching is mandatory (a16), and only three religious minorities are recognised, excluding others from the protection of Article 27.
minorities.note_fa: استفاده از زبان‌های محلی و قومی در رسانه‌ها و تدریس ادبیات آنها در کنار فارسی آزاد است (اصل ۱۵)، مذاهب اهل سنت محترم شمرده شده‌اند (اصل ۱۲) و اقلیت‌های شناخته‌شده نماینده دارند (اصل ۶۴). اما زبان اسناد و کتب درسی الزاماً فارسی است، تدریس عربی اجباری است (اصل ۱۶) و تنها سه اقلیت دینی شناخته می‌شوند.

family.quote: همه قوانین ... باید در جهت آسان کردن تشکیل خانواده، پاسداری از قداست آن و استواری روابط خانوادگی بر پایه حقوق و اخلاق اسلامی باشد
family.note_en: Article 10 protects the family and requires laws to facilitate its formation, but expressly on the basis of "Islamic law and ethics", and Article 21 conditions women's family rights on Islamic criteria. Free and full consent to marriage, a minimum marriage age and equality of spouses during and at dissolution of marriage are nowhere guaranteed.
family.note_fa: اصل ۱۰ خانواده را واحد بنیادی می‌داند و قوانین را موظف به تسهیل تشکیل آن می‌کند، اما صریحاً «بر پایه حقوق و اخلاق اسلامی»؛ اصل ۲۱ نیز حقوق خانوادگی زن را مشروط به موازین اسلامی می‌کند. رضایت آزادانه و کامل برای ازدواج، حداقل سن ازدواج و برابری زوجین در هنگام ازدواج و انحلال آن تضمین نشده است.

children.quote: حمایت مادران، بالخصوص در دوران بارداری و حضانت فرزند، و حمایت از کودکان بی‌سرپرست.
children.note_en: Only fragments appear: support for mothers and for children without guardians (a21.2), custody to fit mothers where there is no "shar'i guardian" (a21.5), and free schooling (a30). The best interests principle, protection from violence, juvenile justice guarantees, a ban on capital punishment for minors and birth registration are all absent.
children.note_fa: تنها اجزای پراکنده‌ای وجود دارد: حمایت از مادران و کودکان بی‌سرپرست (بند ۲ اصل ۲۱)، سپردن قیمومت به مادر شایسته در صورت نبود «ولی شرعی» (بند ۵) و آموزش رایگان (اصل ۳۰). اصل مصلحت عالیه کودک، حمایت از کودک در برابر خشونت، دادرسی ویژه نوجوانان، منع اعدام کودکان و ثبت ولادت غایب‌اند.

disability.note_en: Disability appears only as a social-insurance category ("ازکارافتادگی") in Article 29; there is no provision on non-discrimination, accessibility, legal capacity or inclusion of persons with disabilities.
disability.note_fa: معلولیت تنها به‌عنوان یکی از عناوین بیمه‌ای («ازکارافتادگی») در اصل ۲۹ آمده است؛ هیچ حکمی درباره منع تبعیض، دسترس‌پذیری، اهلیت قانونی یا مشارکت افراد دارای معلولیت وجود ندارد.

work.quote: هر کس حق دارد شغلی را که بدان مایل است و مخالف اسلام و مصالح عمومی و حقوق دیگران نیست برگزیند
work.note_en: Free choice of occupation is granted but only for work "not contrary to Islam and public interests" (a28); Article 29 makes social security a universal right and Article 43 promises full employment and limits on working hours. Equal pay for equal work, safe conditions and independent unions or the right to strike are not guaranteed.
work.note_fa: آزادی انتخاب شغل تنها برای کاری که «مخالف اسلام و مصالح عمومی» نباشد شناخته شده است (اصل ۲۸)؛ اصل ۲۹ تأمین اجتماعی را حقی همگانی می‌داند و اصل ۴۳ اشتغال کامل و تنظیم ساعات کار را وعده می‌دهد. اما دستمزد برابر برای کار برابر، شرایط ایمن کار و اتحادیه‌های مستقل و حق اعتصاب تضمین نشده‌اند.

living_standard.quote: داشتن مسکن متناسب با نیاز، حق هر فرد و خانواده ایرانی است.
living_standard.note_en: Article 43(1) lists housing, food, clothing, health care and education as basic needs to be secured for all, and Article 31 makes adequate housing a right, but the housing right is expressly limited to "every Iranian individual and family", and the whole economic order must stay "within the bounds of Islamic law" (a44) and Article 4.
living_standard.note_fa: بند ۱ اصل ۴۳ مسکن، خوراک، پوشاک، بهداشت و آموزش را از نیازهای اساسی «برای همه» می‌داند و اصل ۳۱ مسکن متناسب را حق می‌شناسد، اما این حق صریحاً به «هر فرد و خانواده ایرانی» محدود شده و کل نظام اقتصادی باید در «محدوده قوانین اسلام» (اصل ۴۴) و اصل ۴ بماند.

health.quote: نیاز به خدمات بهداشتی‌درمانی و مراقبت های پزشکی به صورت بیمه و غیره، حقی است همگانی
health.note_en: Article 29 declares access to health and medical care a universal right and obliges the state to fund it for every individual in the country; Article 43(1) counts health and treatment among the basic needs to be met, and Article 50 protects the environment.
health.note_fa: اصل ۲۹ برخورداری از خدمات بهداشتی‌درمانی را «حقی همگانی» می‌داند و دولت را موظف می‌کند آن را برای یک‌یک افراد کشور تأمین کند؛ بند ۱ اصل ۴۳ نیز بهداشت و درمان را جزو نیازهای اساسی می‌شمارد و اصل ۵۰ از محیط زیست حفاظت می‌کند.

education.quote: دولت موظف است وسایل آموزش و پرورش رایگان را برای همه ملت تا پایان دوره متوسطه فراهم سازد
education.note_en: Free education to the end of secondary school and expansion of free higher education are promised (a30, a3.3), but the entitlement runs to "the whole nation" (citizens), Arabic instruction is compulsory in all classes and fields (a16), educational content is bound by Islamic criteria (a4), and parents' liberty to choose their children's moral and religious education is not recognised.
education.note_fa: آموزش رایگان تا پایان متوسطه و گسترش رایگان تحصیلات عالی وعده داده شده است (اصول ۳۰ و ۳ بند ۳)، اما این حق به «همه ملت» محدود است، تدریس عربی در همه کلاس‌ها و رشته‌ها اجباری است (اصل ۱۶)، محتوای آموزش تابع موازین اسلامی (اصل ۴) است و حق والدین در انتخاب تربیت دینی و اخلاقی فرزندان به رسمیت شناخته نشده است.

culture.note_en: There is no right to take part in cultural life, to enjoy scientific progress or to protection of authors' moral and material interests; the text only sets state duties to found research centres and encourage researchers (a3.4) and allows local-language literature in schools (a15).
culture.note_fa: حقی برای مشارکت در حیات فرهنگی، بهره‌مندی از پیشرفت علمی یا حمایت از منافع مادی و معنوی پدیدآورندگان پیش‌بینی نشده است؛ متن تنها وظایف دولت در تأسیس مراکز تحقیق و تشویق محققان (بند ۴ اصل ۳) و تدریس ادبیات محلی (اصل ۱۵) را بیان می‌کند.

emergency.quote: برقراری حکومت نظامی ممنوع است. در حالت جنگ و شرایط اضطراری نظیر آن، دولت حق دارد با تصویب مجلس شورای اسلامی موقتا محدودیت های ضروری را برقرار نماید
emergency.note_en: Article 79 bans martial law and caps emergency restrictions at thirty days with parliamentary approval, a real procedural safeguard, but it lists no non-derogable rights as ICCPR.4.2 requires, and Article 68 allows elections to be suspended nationwide during war.
emergency.note_fa: اصل ۷۹ حکومت نظامی را ممنوع و محدودیت‌های اضطراری را به سی روز با تصویب مجلس محدود می‌کند که تضمینی شکلی است، اما هیچ فهرستی از حقوق غیرقابل‌تعلیق مطابق ماده ۴(۲) میثاق ندارد و اصل ۶۸ امکان تعطیلی انتخابات در سراسر کشور را در زمان جنگ می‌دهد.

atrocity_crimes.note_en: Genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes are not mentioned, and no duty to prevent or punish them or to deny immunity to officials is created; Article 107's statement that the Leader is equal before the law is the only related clause, with no enforcement mechanism.
atrocity_crimes.note_fa: نسل‌کشی، جنایات علیه بشریت و جنایات جنگی ذکر نشده‌اند و هیچ تکلیفی به پیشگیری، مجازات یا نفی مصونیت مقامات پیش‌بینی نشده است؛ تنها جمله «رهبر در برابر قوانین با سایر افراد کشور مساوی است» در اصل ۱۰۷ مرتبط است که سازوکار اجرایی ندارد.
